title: A piloted Rotor round lands where its tracer ends: its straight line is solved against the ground and the walls before it leaves, the head stops exactly on that point and the burst and ring are put there the frame after; a ground aim is no longer lifted, so the round lands on the reticle's point
context: Owner, playtest of b8e560d (2026-09-25): "Rotor bullet tracing; it goes straight whereas the planet is curved, so the trace does not impact at the same point. The trace should land on the same path as the impact." Since 2026-09-14-piloted-rounds-fly-straight-from-the-barrel a piloted round flies a straight 3D line and its tracer's head is the round's true point, but its end of flight was left from the surface-following round: the range came from rayToTerrain, the lance's march, which stops a quarter of a cell underground and returns one 0.2-cell step back (or 1.35x range in the air); the burst went on the round's last point dropped radially onto r = 1 and the ring on that cell's centre; and the round was killed in the update that moved its head, so its last point was never drawn. A ground aim point was lifted 0.3 cell like a body's centre, so a round aimed at the ground flew on past the reticle.
outcome: src/domain/round-path.js (pure) owns where a straight line from a gun meets the planet: roundEnd is the exact first crossing, r = 1 by the gunship's own aimOnSphere, rock solved on its top at r = 1 + wallHeight or bisected to the side it enters, null when still in the air at maxLen, the gun's own cell never stopping it; flyStraight is the round's step, clamped so the head sits exactly on the end, with the landing reported one call later so the frame that draws the head there comes first; marchToTerrain is the controller's rayToTerrain moved unchanged (the lance's beam, its steering in a seat and its line-of-sight gate, and the reach of the automatic and lobbed rounds keep it). In src/td-tab.js a straight round's range is its end's length; endTowerShot puts the burst on the end point and centres the ring on that point (warnRing takes an optional point; it snapped to the cell's centre, half a cell off in the first still), and a round still in the air goes out with no impact; a ground aim point is no longer lifted (a body's centre still is) and the pilot's aimPoint is roundEnd from the optic, so a round aimed at the ground lands on the reticle's point; pilotHits counts a round that hit and flew on; state().pilotTracerGap is the widest distance from a piloted tracer's last drawn head to its burst, in metres, and --story-world asserts it under 0.5 m (0.05 cell) after the Rotor-kill burst. td-tab 9436 -> 9417 lines, 536519 -> 536327 bytes, 18 -> 17 lines over 500 characters. Left for later: the automatic Rotor's round still flies along the surface at 2 m, its tracer starting there and not at the muzzle, its range ray starting 0.2 cell up and never dropping below the rock threshold, so automatic rounds fly through the 4 m walls, and its burst still drops onto r = 1 under its head; a piloted round overlapping one body for several frames damages it each frame and counts each as one of its three (up to three times a round's damage on one multi-hp body: a balance question, not changed); the lance's stop is on its straight line while its beam is drawn on the great circle at the muzzle's height; the aim line comes from the optic while the PoV camera sits 0.34 cell behind and 0.12 above it, so a close ground impact shows above the cross (33 px at 1.6 cells, 10 px at 2.4, 1 px at 3.2 on a 900 px view).
alternatives: Keeping the lance's march for the round's range and only moving the burst to the tracer's head: the head would still stop a quarter cell underground or one frame short, and the point was never solved, only sampled.
Solving open ground by marching and bisecting too: aimOnSphere is the gunship's exact answer already, and the test holds the round to it bit for bit.
A small puff in the air at a round's range: left out; the tracer simply goes out, since nothing is there to hit.
evidence: test/round-path.mjs: a muzzle 0.69 cell up aimed at the ground 3 cells out lands on r = 1 exactly where aimOnSphere does and on the aimed point; a level ray over 4.86 cells ends in the air at maxLen; rock through its top at 1 + wallHeight, through its side at the cell edge, a sliver short of the ground crossing; the gun's own cell; at 30, 60 and 144 Hz the last head drawn is exactly the end point and the landing is the next call. 12 of 12 mutants of the module fail it.
marchToTerrain against the original rayToTerrain text on 60,000 random rays over a random board: 0 differ (11,564 wall, 14,485 ground, 33,951 air).

Tracer probe from frozen copies (stage 1, the Rotor held on open ground 1.6/2.4/3.2 cells ahead, 32 rounds each, three runs of each build): before, last drawn tracer head to burst 3.5-5.0 m (means 3.9-4.6 m), bursts 12-23 m past the reticle's point on average (up to 27 m), the old aim point 1.1-2.4 m underground; after, 96-97 landings a run, widest 0.000012 m (the Float32 vertex), every burst on the reticle's point. PoV and third-view stills of both builds: before, the rounds run on past the cross and the puffs land well beyond it, the rings on the cells' centres off to one side; after, the tracers end in the ring at the reticle.
--story-world with the old td-tab and the new assertion fails it (28 rounds, widest 9.05 m); with the change it passes end to end (29 rounds, 17 hit, widest 0.000019 m).

Through scripts/browser-lock.sh from a frozen copy of the committed tree: --story-world, --grow, --quiver-frame, --missile-parity, --seats, --gunship and the default suite pass (the default suite's first run stopped at docs-roadmap because the copy lacked ROADMAP.md; with it, 48 steps pass).
npm test (153 programs), npm run check, npm run build; commit 524dd32c on branch tracer-impact.
